title: Trace-norm commutator conjecture for matrix functions
statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be positive semidefinite $d\times d$ matrices with $\operatorname{Tr}A=a$ and $\operatorname{Tr}B=b$. For a function $f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}$, define

$$
F(x)=\int_0^x f(y)\,dy.
$$

**Trace-norm commutator conjecture.** For certain functions $f$ still to be determined, there exists a constant $c$ independent of $d$ such that

$$
\lVert[B,f(A+B)]\rVert_1\leq c\bigl(F(a+b)-F(a)-F(b)\bigr).
$$

This is presented as a natural generalisation of a previously discussed trace-norm inequality for commutators. The admissible class of functions $f$ and the optimal constant are left open in the source.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1411.0680

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2014).
source_name: Michaël Mariën, Koenraad M. R. Audenaert, Karel Van Acoleyen and Frank Verstraete, “Entanglement Rates and the Stability of the Area Law for the Entanglement Entropy”, arXiv:1411.0680 (2014).
